title: Nine Months of Pencil
subtitle: 四季节令 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 四季节令（自然生态·四季与节令）
meta: 主题语境：四季节令（自然生态·四季与节令）　|　核心词汇：calendar　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 calendar 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 my mother was sent to keep ① a calendar she could not read, and she said the reading was the whole of the lesson. The ② calendar, meaning the page and not the year, was nine months deep and was marked by whoever came last; a calendar, she said, is the only thing in a kitchen that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ calendar in that kitchen had the same pencil, and the ④ calendar at the door, meaning the one the farmer kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever marked properly. A calendar, my grandmother said, is nine parts pencil and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the pencil is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ calendar was the whole of the year, meaning the seasons it ordered and not the page. The ⑥ calendar, meaning the year and not any of that, is the only thing in a house that everybody crosses off and nobody questions; a calendar, he said, is either something you keep or the only word that means both a page and a year. She said the year is the part they remember.

By 1969 the ⑦ calendar had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the pencil. The ⑧ calendar of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine months and eleven years of marking; a calendar, she said, is either the one at the door or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ calendar I remember is the one at the door, which was kept in 1974 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ calendar, my grandmother said in 1978, is the only thing that improves by being marked; every calendar, she said, is a year that has agreed to look like a page. She said the year was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 日历（指那张纸本身，与年相对）
C. 固定搭配：keep a calendar 记／使用日历
D. n. 日历（指厨房里每一本）
E. n. 日历（指门边那一本）
F. n. 日历（抽象：它编排的那一年）
G. n. 那一年（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a calendar she could not read
The calendar, meaning the page and not the year
calendar was the whole of the year
the calendar had become a photograph in a report
The calendar of the whole thing
A calendar, my grandmother said in 1978

answers.why: keep a calendar 意为“记／使用日历”，1953 年母亲被派去记一份她看不懂的日历。
calendar 意为“日历”，指那张纸本身而不是年，记了九个月，由最后走的人画记号。
calendar 指厨房里每一本日历，每一本都配着同一支铅笔。
calendar 指门边那一本（农夫用的那一本），是唯一有人认真画过记号的。
calendar 意为“日历”，抽象指它编排的那一年，父亲说 calendar 就是那一年的全部。
calendar 为抽象用法，指那一年本身，是屋子里人人都划掉、却没人质疑的东西。
calendar 意为“日历、历法”，到 1969 年这本 calendar 成了报告里的一张照片。
calendar 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九个月和十一年的画记号。
calendar 意为“日历”，我记得的是门边那一本，1974 年留着，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
calendar 为抽象总称，祖母说日历是唯一会因为被画上记号而变好的东西。

The calendar at the door, meaning the one the farmer kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever marked properly.
My father said calendar was the whole of the year, meaning the seasons it ordered and not the page.
